note: Why a personality decision did not run, or ran without personality turning it, in the trait-wiring audit (docs/reports/trait-wiring-2026-10-20.md). One row per decision with a gap; the matrix (scripts/traits/trait-wiring-matrix.ts) joins them. A row is removed when its fix lands.

corruption.offer.why: Ran 4,407 times in the election-window audit (Parkway, Missouri, seed e6ff0d60d6bc, window 2025-12-03 to 2026-12-03): at a lobbyist's first meeting with a member on a bill with employer costs (src/core2/modules/interest-groups.ts:396) and at contract awards (src/core2/modules/contracts.ts:150). Every offer was declined in the drawn, flat and mirrored worlds: the yes score never beats corruptionHonestPull 3 (src/core2/modules/corruption.ts:322), so personality never turns one.
corruption.offer.fix: Weigh the stake against the official's own money need and calibrate the honesty pull from the honesty-humility effect size (pool item people-corruption-honest-pull-calibrated).

corruption.take.class: trigger needs a record nobody writes
corruption.take.why: Weighed only after an offer says yes (src/core2/modules/corruption.ts:187). None of the 4,407 offers in the election window did; a declined offer returns at :220 before any crime row is written.

corruption.tell.class: trigger needs a record nobody writes
corruption.tell.why: Weighed only for a taken bribe: when a party's closeness to the other falls (src/core2/modules/corruption.ts:363, from onRelationshipChange) and when a told listener weighs going to the press (:437). Both need a crime row with taken true, and none was written.

justice.report.class: trigger needs a record nobody writes
justice.report.why: Justice's only source of crimes is the corruption table: the daily intake reads refused offers (src/core2/modules/justice.ts:250-260) and onTold reads a party's telling (:1465-1475). A declined offer writes no crime row (src/core2/modules/corruption.ts:220), so none arrived; the report's reasons are read at justice.ts:283.

justice.prosecute.class: trigger needs a record nobody writes

justice.plea.class: trigger needs a record nobody writes

press.tip.class: trigger needs a record nobody writes
press.tip.why: Needs a crime.told event for a taken bribe (src/core2/modules/press.ts:275, :2081); the tip is weighed at :2144. leakToReporter (:2245) is the player's own leak.

recalls.organize.why: Only a city or county ordinance taking effect starts one (src/core2/modules/recalls.ts:83 onEvent, :349 weighOrdinance), and it returns before weighing anyone where the state's municipal doctrine allows no petition recall (:338, recallRule is null) and where the state requires grounds (:368). Over the 56 places (resolveMunicipalRecallRule), 14 allow a recall without grounds, 8 only for cause and 34 not at all (17 whose state prohibits it, 15 with no state row that take the national estimate of prohibited, 2 judicial-trial states). The election-window place is one of the 15, so no organizer was ever weighed.
recalls.organize.fix: Let a reported scandal or crime start a for-cause recall where the state requires grounds, and read each of the 34 places' own rule instead of the national estimate of prohibited (pool item gov-recall-for-cause-start).

recalls.sign.why: Follows an organizer: startRecall (src/core2/modules/recalls.ts:480) weighs each signer at :502.

recalls.vote.why: Needs a recall on the ballot after a petition with enough signatures (src/core2/modules/recalls.ts:565-616).

ballot-measures.vote.class: runs only in an election window
ballot-measures.vote.why: Runs on a measure's election date. The default audit year (January 20, 2025 to January 20, 2026) holds none (the earliest measure in data/elections/ballot-measures.json is June 16, 2026). With TRAIT_AUDIT_ELECTION=1 it ran 277 times (Parkway, Missouri, seed e6ff0d60d6bc, window 2025-12-03 to 2026-12-03; first call 2026-08-04).
ballot-measures.vote.fix: None in the engine: audit the place's own election window (TRAIT_AUDIT_ELECTION=1 in scripts/traits/trait-wiring-audit.ts).

voting.turnout.class: runs only in an election window
voting.turnout.why: Runs on an election day. Most places hold no election in the default audit year (January 20, 2025 to January 20, 2026). With TRAIT_AUDIT_ELECTION=1 it ran 2,681 times (Parkway, Missouri, seed e6ff0d60d6bc, window 2025-12-03 to 2026-12-03; first call 2026-04-28).
voting.turnout.fix: None in the engine: audit the place's own election window (TRAIT_AUDIT_ELECTION=1 in scripts/traits/trait-wiring-audit.ts).

voting.back-incumbent.class: runs only in an election window
voting.back-incumbent.why: Same as voting.turnout: 12,324 calls in the election window (Parkway, Missouri, seed e6ff0d60d6bc, window 2025-12-03 to 2026-12-03; first call 2026-04-28).
voting.back-incumbent.fix: None in the engine: audit the place's own election window (TRAIT_AUDIT_ELECTION=1 in scripts/traits/trait-wiring-audit.ts).

voting.exit-poll.class: runs only in an election window
voting.exit-poll.why: Same as voting.turnout: 486 calls in the election window (Parkway, Missouri, seed e6ff0d60d6bc, window 2025-12-03 to 2026-12-03; first call 2026-11-03).
voting.exit-poll.fix: None in the engine: audit the place's own election window (TRAIT_AUDIT_ELECTION=1 in scripts/traits/trait-wiring-audit.ts).

campaigns.answer-poll.class: runs only in an election window
campaigns.answer-poll.why: Runs once a campaign has set aside enough for a poll (src/core2/modules/campaigns.ts, pollFund against pollMinimumInterviews). With TRAIT_AUDIT_ELECTION=1 it ran 12,215 times (Parkway, Missouri, seed e6ff0d60d6bc, window 2025-12-03 to 2026-12-03; first call 2026-06-25); no local campaign in four default-year places raised enough.
campaigns.answer-poll.fix: Weight calibrated from the adults of a drawn town (campaigns.traits.test.ts); audit the place's own election window (TRAIT_AUDIT_ELECTION=1).

offices.accept-appointment.why: Weighed only when a city, county or township seat falls vacant and the post fills by appointment: fillVacancy's appoint (src/core2/modules/offices.ts:1135, decision read at :1162) offers the post only to a city, county or township seat, only under a vacancy rule that appoints (successor, appointment, or appointment-then-special, called at :1216, :1218 and :1238), and only when no named successor is given first (:1190). A vacancy needs the serving official to die or move away; none did in the election window.
offices.accept-appointment.fix: Audit a drawn year that holds a local vacancy filled by appointment (traits-accept-appointment-vacancy-proof).

constituent-cases.handle-case.why: The official's own read (src/core2/modules/constituent-cases.ts:437, ownCaseDecision) runs only for an official with no staffer: officeHandles hands every case to a staffer first (:451). Ran 2 times in one election-window run (first 2026-01-09) and none in a later one.
constituent-cases.handle-case.fix: The official decides every case first and the staffer carries it out (traits-wire-integrity, PR 5715); its circumstances vary with traits-integrity-cases-vary.

conversation.believe-claim.why: Read only when the player's line makes a claim: say (src/director/conversation.ts:2295) asks doubtsClaim (:2272, decision read at :2281) of each hearer at :2346 for the player's lie.
conversation.believe-claim.fix: Read it where people pass on claims to each other (speech retell, news pass-on) (pool item traits-wire-civic).

conversation.reply-reach.why: Read only to rank the replies offered to the player in a conversation the player opens (src/director/conversation.ts:2003, :2036) and in the player's speech builder (src/director/speech-builder.ts:281, from src/bench/campaign.ts).
conversation.reply-reach.fix: Player-only by design; covered by the player's conversations.

scene-talk.move.why: Read only when the director composes a scene with a purpose for the player (src/director/scene-talk.ts): the asker's answer and the reply the player's character leans toward.
scene-talk.move.fix: Player-only by design; covered by scene-talk.test.ts on a generated town.

bring-it-up.blame.why: Read only when a person raises a change in a conversation the player opens: leansToBlame (src/director/bring-it-up.ts:125, decision read at :133) is reached from believedCause (:141), which bringItUp (:206) calls from the bench handler (src/bench/handler.ts:382) and the grading tool.

press.dig.why: Two routes. An interview answer whose move is a lie schedules the reporter's check (src/core2/modules/press.ts:1773-1780, read at :1845), but candidateAnswers gives every candidate who is not the player the move 'plain' (:1929, :1935), so only the player's interview can lie: 168 interviews were accepted in the election window and none dug. A tipped crime reaches the dig at :2166, which needs a taken bribe.
press.dig.fix: Let a simulated candidate whose stated position contradicts their recorded vote answer with the lie move, from their own honesty, ties and the record; the reporter's check then runs from the press engine's own rule (pool item press-world-candidates-answer-from-record).

estates.will.why: Runs when someone with an estate dies (src/core2/estates.ts, willOf): 5 and 1 times in the two played years, and 3 times in an election window (first 2026-10-08). Weighed for every adult 55 or older in Haledon, New Jersey as if at death, the age term puts all 858 over the line with temperament off, against the study's 37.4% (Ryser et al. 2026, Swiss adults 55+), so no weight can reach the study's odds of 1.42.
estates.will.fix: A will-making rate by age from research for the age term, then the weight (people-estates-will-trust-rates); the audit's witness of the retained decision or estate record is traits-audit-will-record-proof.

office-day-state.clemency.why: Weighed on a governor's weekly review day (src/core2/office-day-state.ts:422-427, read at :761-770) only when clemencyDue (:468) finds a state prisoner in custody (src/core2/modules/justice.ts:1305). Custody comes only from a sentence (justice.ts:932, imprison), and justice's only source of crimes is the corruption table, which wrote none, so no governor had a petition to review.
office-day-state.clemency.fix: Same as corruption.offer: once any crime reaches a sentence, the governor's review has someone to weigh (pool item people-corruption-honest-pull-calibrated).

housing.buy-home.why: No study of personality and becoming a homeowner was found, so the weight stays at the general 1 and the fits against an assumed 1.49 between the thirds are kept here: Holualoa, Hawaii 2.05 (341 weighings, 3 buyers, odds ratio 1.68); Peacham, Vermont none reachable (140 weighings, 1 purchase); place key 2371780 0.1 (791 weighings, 16 buyers, odds ratio 11 at weight 1). A renter now weighs the share of the down payment it is short, from none to all of it (homeBuyReasons, src/core2/modules/housing.ts), instead of a log that ran to minus thirty, and buying sits 0.6 below renting before cost, so households that can pay the down payment sit within reach of a lean. Counted renter households do not buy at all yet (pool item world-counted-renters-buy), so this decision has no counted counterpart.
housing.buy-home.fix: A homeownership study with a trait number, and the counted renters' purchase path.

jobs.apply.why: Kanfer et al. 2001 give only the range of correlations across all antecedents of job search behavior (-.15 to .46; the abstract has no per-trait number), so the decision keeps the general weight of 1 (the pool item's rule for a decision with no study). A seeker's push to apply eases with the weeks looked (applyNeed, src/core2/modules/jobs.ts), so some applications sit near waiting and temperament turns some of them.
jobs.apply.fix: Read Kanfer et al.'s per-trait correlations from the paper's tables and fit the weight to them (research-jobs-apply-kanfer-per-trait).

drives.respond.why: Personality turned none of 1,471 drive responses in Ely, Nevada at any weight up to 8: the drive's own strength separates the options. No study gives a size (neuroticism and rumination is the direction).
drives.respond.fix: None until the options score closer or a study gives a size; the general trait weight of 1 stands.

school.attend.why: Children attend 99.95% of school days (10,587 kept weighings, Ely, Nevada); personality turns none below a weight of 1 and at 1 the third least inclined misses at 11 times the odds. Real chronic absence is far higher and follows illness, family and poverty, which the school choice does not read (src/core2/modules/school.ts:149). Poropat 2009 (conscientiousness r 0.19) measures performance, not attendance.
school.attend.fix: Give the school choice the child's illness and the household's circumstances, then calibrate.

life.daily-act.why: Personality turned 14.8% of 29,520 daily-activity picks at the general trait weight of 1. Studies of extraversion and time spent socializing (Mehl et al. 2006) report no extractable coefficient, so the general weight stands.
life.daily-act.fix: Calibrate when a study gives a size for extraversion and social time.

campaigns.volunteer.why: Most adults a campaign reaches share one reason total: no warmth toward the candidate yet, no tie, no family link and no work hours (src/core2/modules/campaigns.ts volunteerReason). Where the yes line falls inside that pile, temperament alone sorts them, so one town's odds ratio between the thirds of lean runs from about 1 to over 30 (Red Cliff, Colorado, 424 calls: 34.6 at a one-in-twenty yes share, against Mondak et al.'s 2.41).
campaigns.volunteer.fix: Give the volunteer choice the person's own free time, interest in the race and agreement with the platform, then calibrate the weight.

voting.stand-again.why: standsAgain (src/core2/modules/voting.ts:319) is read only from fileStandingCandidates (:1126), which returns at :1132 whenever the candidacy module is installed, and candidacy owns every incumbent's decision to run or stay out (its own decision, candidacy.run). Every played world installs candidacy, so the call at :1196 is never reached, in the election window as in the default year.
voting.stand-again.fix: Fold the age term (standAgainReason, voting.ts:334) into candidacy's reasons for an incumbent and delete standsAgain and the stand-in branch, or measure the decision only in a world built without candidacy (pool item elections-stand-again-dead-with-candidacy).

appointments.weigh.class: runs only at the opening and on a vacancy
appointments.weigh.why: The appointer's loyalty against merit (src/core2/appointments.ts:56) is read whenever a post is filled. The town's department heads and the state's cabinet are filled when the executive module opens (src/core2/modules/executive.ts:151-152), before the audit's probe is on; afterward only a department head who dies or moves away (executive.ts:1168-1172) or a newly seated governor (:1197) fills one, and neither happened in the election window.
appointments.weigh.fix: Count the opening's calls apart from the played year, with an appointment's record id (traits-audit-opening-appointments).

housing.settle-arrears.class: counted households have no arrears of their own
housing.settle-arrears.why: Runs each month for every full household with rent owed (src/core2/modules/housing.ts, review calls settleArrears and writes a `settlements` row per household and month; South Paris, Maine: 17 rows, 8 of them with a payment; Arroyo Hondo, New Mexico: 4 rows, none paid) and once when a counted household behind on rent is filled in. It does not run monthly for counted households: their rent is paid from a pool shared by place, and the pool repays its group's arrears every month before anything else (src/core2/counted-money.ts, chargeGroups asks rent plus the group's arrears), so there is no moment when a counted household holds cash and chooses between settling and letting it lapse. Households behind on rent seldom hold cash beyond a month's living, so most weighings paid nothing. Willingness is a share, so the general weight of 1 stands with no study.
housing.settle-arrears.fix: Give counted households cash and arrears of their own (stopgap SG-WORLD-housing-counted-rent), then weigh them monthly like the full ones.

legislature.poison-pill.why: movesPill (src/core2/modules/legislature.ts:3335) is asked only after floorAmendments (:3145) finds a bill that would pass (:3283), an opponent, and a section of the opponent's own that a majority of the roll would adopt and that leaves fewer than the votes needed (:3294-3319). No bill got that far in the election window; which of the guards held was not measured.
legislature.poison-pill.fix: Measure which guard holds across a session; if the section search is too narrow (pillCandidates), widen it so a contested bill reaches the member's own decision (pool item gov-poison-pill-guards-measured).

relationships.fall-out.class: trigger needs a record nobody writes
relationships.fall-out.why: Runs when a relationship change carries negative hours (src/core2/state.ts:1068, src/core2/closeness.ts:259). Two engines write them: a grudge drive's confrontation (src/core2/modules/drives.ts:1809), offered only against a living person (:1583) while the drive's target is the employer, landlord or closed business it blames (src/core2/data/drives.json:685-694), so no confrontation was offered; and a taken bribe the official voted against (src/core2/modules/corruption.ts:545), which needs a taken bribe.
relationships.fall-out.fix: Let a grudge drive name the person behind the organization (the manager who fired, the landlord who evicted) so a confrontation can be offered; the bribe route follows corruption.offer (pool item people-grudge-confront-person).

contracts.award.why: Each member of a government's body ranks every bid by price against their tie to the firm's owner (src/core2/modules/contracts.ts), and temperament moves weight between the two: 1,450 and 1,740 calls in the two played years, with no yes or no for scripts/traits/trait-calibrate.ts to fit against Pletzer et al. 2020.
contracts.award.fix: A ranking calibration: how often the most rule-bending third picks the known firm over the lowest bid against the least.

estates.trust.why: Runs at death (src/core2/estates.ts, trustOf): 14 and 13 times in the two played years. Weighed for the 832 adults 55 or older with savings in Haledon, New Jersey, the wealth term keeps 98% far below the line, and temperament turns none at any weight up to 1, against the study's odds of 1.34.
estates.trust.fix: A trust-holding rate by wealth from research for the wealth term, then the weight (people-estates-will-trust-rates).

renewal.plan-child.why: A couple's case for planning a child (src/core2/births-plan.ts, birthCircumstances) sits 3.6 to 18.3 below waiting in nine of ten reviews (Haledon, New Jersey, seed fc8bf1311d0f, 384 reviews), while temperament spans about plus or minus 0.4, so at the general weight it turned none. scripts/traits/trait-calibrate.ts fits 7.05 there (odds 1.74 against the study's 1.93), but at that weight the share of reviews that plan a child rises from 1.8% to 2.6%, about 40% more births; in Kenvir, Kentucky (32bb83941552, 210 reviews) no weight reaches it.
renewal.plan-child.fix: Re-center the waiting side against the births rate, then set the weight (traits-plan-child-weight-recentered).

business.open-location.why: Owners never open a second location in 282 weighings: the expand score sits 6 to 9 below keeping (baseline -3, room term, src/core2/modules/business.ts:1551), and no study of owners' expansion by personality has a number.
business.open-location.fix: Find a study of owner expansion and calibrate the expand baseline against it.

business.owner-draw.why: No study of owners' draws by personality has a number, so the decision keeps the general weight of 1 (the pool item's rule for a decision with no study). An owner weighs the business's cash against a month of everything it pays out, not only payroll, so 40 to 50 percent of weighings sit within a point of keeping, and temperament turns some of them.
business.owner-draw.fix: A study that reports owners' withdrawals by trait.

jobs.raise-for-opening.why: How much of the affordable raise an owner gives an unfilled seat is a share (open-handedness times what the seat can carry), not a two-way choice, so scripts/traits/trait-calibrate.ts cannot fit it. Thielmann, Spadaro and Balliet 2020 (Psychological Bulletin 146(1), Table 8) give the nearest size: agreeableness .08 and honesty-humility .09 with what an ultimatum proposer offers (data/research/trait-effect-sizes.json, jobs.raise-for-opening), a lab game with students, so the general weight of 1 stands.
jobs.raise-for-opening.fix: A study of employers' wage offers by trait, or a fit of the share against the correlation of .08.

jobs.review-worker.why: Zimmerman 2008 (Personnel Psychology 61(2), a meta-analysis of personality and turnover) gives only the direction in the text read (conscientiousness and agreeableness best predict actual turnover), so the decision keeps the general weight of 1 (the pool item's rule for a decision with no study number); a fit to an assumed 1.2 per standard deviation is not used.
jobs.review-worker.fix: Read the per-trait sizes from the paper's tables and fit the weight to them (research-jobs-turnover-zimmerman-per-trait).

jobs.start-looking.why: Zimmerman 2008 (Personnel Psychology 61(2), a meta-analysis of personality and turnover) gives only the direction in the text read (emotional stability best predicts intentions to quit), so the decision keeps the general weight of 1 (the pool item's rule for a decision with no study number); a fit to an assumed 1.2 per standard deviation is not used.
jobs.start-looking.fix: Read the per-trait sizes from the paper's tables and fit the weight to them (research-jobs-turnover-zimmerman-per-trait).

jobs.accept-offer.why: Zimmerman 2008 (Personnel Psychology 61(2), a meta-analysis of personality and turnover) gives only the direction in the text read and Kanfer et al. 2001 (Journal of Applied Psychology 86(5)) give only the range of correlations across all antecedents of job search behavior (-.15 to .46) in the abstract read, so the decision keeps the general weight of 1 (the pool item's rule for a decision with no study number); a fit to an assumed 1.2 per standard deviation is not used.
jobs.accept-offer.fix: Read the per-trait sizes from the paper's tables and fit the weight to them (research-jobs-turnover-zimmerman-per-trait).

jobs.counted-retire.why: No retirement-timing study with a number by trait was found, so the decision keeps the general weight of 1 (the pool item's rule for a decision with no study number); a fit to an assumed 1.2 per standard deviation is not used.
jobs.counted-retire.fix: Read the per-trait sizes from the paper's tables and fit the weight to them (research-jobs-turnover-zimmerman-per-trait).

jobs.counted-look.why: Zimmerman 2008 (Personnel Psychology 61(2), a meta-analysis of personality and turnover) gives only the direction in the text read (emotional stability best predicts intentions to quit), so the decision keeps the general weight of 1 (the pool item's rule for a decision with no study number); a fit to an assumed 1.2 per standard deviation is not used.
jobs.counted-look.fix: Read the per-trait sizes from the paper's tables and fit the weight to them (research-jobs-turnover-zimmerman-per-trait).

jobs.counted-apply.why: Kanfer et al. 2001 (Journal of Applied Psychology 86(5)) give only the range of correlations across all antecedents of job search behavior (-.15 to .46) in the abstract read, so the decision keeps the general weight of 1 (the pool item's rule for a decision with no study number); a fit to an assumed 1.2 per standard deviation is not used.
jobs.counted-apply.fix: Read the per-trait sizes from the paper's tables and fit the weight to them (research-jobs-apply-kanfer-per-trait).

jobs.counted-accept.why: Zimmerman 2008 (Personnel Psychology 61(2), a meta-analysis of personality and turnover) gives only the direction in the text read, so the decision keeps the general weight of 1 (the pool item's rule for a decision with no study number); a fit to an assumed 1.2 per standard deviation is not used.
jobs.counted-accept.fix: Read the per-trait sizes from the paper's tables and fit the weight to them (research-jobs-turnover-zimmerman-per-trait).
